newsitem.title: INDIA: Sri Lanka president arrives in India.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka president arrives in India.

text.p: Sri Lankan President Chandrika Bandaranaike Kumaratunga arrived in New Delhi on Tuesday for a week-long private visit but officials said she would also hold talks with Indian leaders on her country's ethnic war.

The United News of India (UNI) said Kumaratunga left for the northwestern desert state of Rajasthan soon after arriving in New Delhi with her family. Sri Lankan diplomats were not immediately available for comment.
Rajasthan, which has a rich tradition of former maharajas, is a leading tourist destination.

Indian newspapers said Kumaratunga's surprise visit followed reports of an offer by the separatist Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE) to hold peace talks with her government through unidentified mediators.
"The president is expected here on a private visit, but she will also meet Indian leaders for informal talks," an Indian official told Reuters earlier.

A Sri Lankan official said earlier his embassy would "make a statement on this matter later", but declined to say more. "We cannot comment on this for security reasons," another Sri Lankan official said.
"My information is that she had planned to take a holiday from the pressures of the civil war in her country," a former Indian diplomat told Reuters on condition of anonymity.
"Of course she will use the occasion to hold informal talks in New Delhi. But nothing more than that should be seen in this visit," he said.

The Hindu newspaper said Sri Lankan Foreign Minister Lakshman Kadirgamar, who arrived in India for a ministerial meeting of the South Asian Association for Regional Cooperation (SAARC) last week, was still in New Delhi.
There was, however, no independent confirmation of Kadirgamar's presence in New Delhi.

India has been closely involved in Sri Lanka's turbulent ethnic crises, providing armed assistance to Colombo in fending off a hardline Sinhalese-led rebellion and later by sending in troops there in a failed attempt to disarm the LTTE.
Tens of thousands of Indian troops were sent to Sri Lanka following a pact between the two governments in 1987.

They were subsequently ordered out of the island nation in 1990 after Colombo began talks with LTTE leader Velupillai Prabhakaran. India's involvement was severely criticised by opposition groups in New Delhi as a "misadventure".
Kumaratunga last visited India for a SAARC summit in May last year.
But she had to cut short her stay at that time after the LTTE shot down an air force plane, signalling a resumption of its 13-year war against Colombo following a brief truce.
